sentenceSets.sentence: Deprived of practice for a full year, the students regressed to habits their teachers had spent two semesters correcting.

answerChoices.reasoning: Close, but this word simply notes a return to a former state, while the sentence stresses that the habits recovered were ones the teachers had worked to eliminate, so ground was lost.
Relapse belongs to illness or addiction, and the sentence describes skills decaying from disuse rather than a condition returning.
This carries a moral flavor of falling away from good conduct, whereas the students' loss here follows from a year without practice, not from weak resolve.
Lapsing suggests letting something quietly expire, but the sentence describes the active reappearance of specific corrected habits.
Too neutral for a sentence that frames the outcome as undoing two semesters of a teacher's work.
Retreat implies a deliberate pulling back, while the change described happens to the students through absence of practice.
This names a general falling off but does not capture the return of particular old habits that the sentence specifies.
Drifting suggests aimless movement, yet the students land back on identifiable habits their teachers had targeted.
Moving forward contradicts a year of lost practice ending in old errors.
Growth is the opposite of returning to habits that had already been corrected.
Persistence would have preserved the corrections rather than surrendering them.

sentenceSets.sentence: Every explanation the philosopher offered depended on some prior cause, so the argument threatened to regress without end.

answerChoices.reasoning: Recurrence means the same thing happening again, but the sentence describes a chain running ever further back toward earlier and earlier causes.
Multiplication would mean more explanations side by side, while the sentence sets them in a single backward line of prior causes.
Extension is directionless, and the sentence specifies movement toward what came before rather than growth in general.
A spiral implies worsening intensity, but the trouble described is purely that each cause demands another one behind it.
Circular reasoning would return to where it started, whereas the sentence has each step reaching to a new prior cause.
Wandering suggests losing the thread, yet the argument here follows a perfectly consistent rule of asking what came before.
Too weak to name the problem, since an argument that simply continued would raise no threat at all.
Branching implies splitting into alternatives, but each explanation in the sentence has exactly one prior cause behind it.
The phrase 'without end' rules out reaching any stopping point.
The sentence presents an unresolved difficulty, not a settlement of one.
Ending is precisely what the endless chain of prior causes prevents.

sentenceSets.sentence: Six months after the therapy ended, two of the patients regressed, losing the motor control they had painstakingly regained.

answerChoices.reasoning: Close, yet the sentence specifies the loss of gains they had already recovered once, a slide back to an earlier condition rather than general decay.
This says only that things got worse, missing the point that the patients fell back to the state the therapy had lifted them out of.
Faltering suggests a stumble or hesitation, but these patients lost the motor control entirely, not momentarily.
Weakening points to diminished strength, while the sentence describes control that had been regained through effort being given back.
A plateau means gains stop accumulating, but here the gains themselves disappear.
Stalling implies progress halting in place, which cannot describe patients who lost ground they had already covered.
Too slight for the outcome described, in which painstakingly regained motor control is gone.
Struggling would mean they were still fighting to hold on, whereas the sentence reports the loss as accomplished.
Recovery is contradicted by the clause about losing what they had regained.
Improvement is the opposite of the outcome the second clause reports.
Holding steady is ruled out by the loss of motor control six months on.
